paragraphs.source_en: How could I, Hashiba Hideyoshi, have gone charging furiously into the attack without even knowing that the enemy had already withdrawn? At the thought, cold sweat broke out all over Hideyoshi—by withdrawing without the slightest hesitation, Ieyasu must have meant to mock him mercilessly. Had Ieyasu been still more ruthless, returned to Komaki one step ahead, and raided Gakuden and Inuyama before Hideyoshi came back, the consequences would have been unthinkable.

paragraphs.source_en: The situation left Hideyoshi utterly at a loss. Unless he found a way through, he would be unable to advance a single step. Korea, the Great Ming—even the loftiest ambitions concerning them could do nothing to relieve the crisis at hand. If even I, Hideyoshi, am trapped in such a predicament, can Ieyasu truly be taking his ease? So Hideyoshi reasoned, yet he still had no means of escaping his predicament.
